title: Strict Apps and IaC Implementation Tasks
beforeImplementation: The governing no-budget goal is active. Use installed Effect 4.0.0-beta.100 and Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.64 source and types as exact authority; never use Effect v3 guidance. Read the active SPEC, plan, structured audit and applicable docs/strict Effect/Alchemy instructions before each slice.
principles: Correct the earliest boundary owner in small vertical slices and update its docs and proof in the same slice.
Keep host callbacks narrow, internal programs typed, Config and secrets Schema-owned, and runtime resources application-owned.
Preserve the thin Alchemy graph, completed deployment evidence, public docs behavior, and report-only authority boundaries.
Do not add compatibility wrappers, generic provider frameworks, helper sprawl, unsafe casts, manual object readers, or raw client escape hatches.
Do not publish, version, deploy, mutate provider state, alter DNS, or copy machine-local checkout paths into durable files.

globalVerification.commitPolicy: Commit each coherent local slice only after focused gates, documentation impact, validation evidence, Changeset or no-Changeset decision, and primary-owner review pass. Do not push or perform an external mutation under this task list.
requiredBeforeFinalPR: fresh terminal audit of apps/docs, alchemy.run.ts, tools/docs-deployment, exports, config, tests, docs, and residual exceptions
evidenceRequired: Exact target revision and installed Effect, TanStack, Fumadocs, Alchemy, Cloudflare, Wrangler, Vite, and Bun versions
Exact installed Effect beta.100 and Alchemy beta.64 API source used by each slice
Before and after call graphs for every moved boundary
Deterministic valid and invalid fixtures for Config, files, JSON, process output, credentials, identity, screenshots, runtime lifetime, and enforcement
Path-evidenced Change required, Preserve, and N/A documentation impact
Changeset path or explicit no-Changeset basis
Bounded validation receipt for each task and one final terminal audit with limitations and non-claims

downstreamArtifactImpact.acceptance: Accepted findings, requirements, tasks, validation, terminal audit, and lifecycle indexes agree.
Five executables use Config, platform services, Schema, closed tagged errors, Effect concurrency/collections, Console, and BunRuntime with deterministic failure proof.
Credential and process ingress is typed, injected, secret-negative, deterministic, and remains report-only.
One application runtime owns managed, injectable proof identity and state while host callbacks, route behavior, and headers remain narrow and tested.
The smallest executable recurrence-prevention control, owner guidance, fixtures, and verification wiring reject the evidenced defects.
Resource graph, stage names, provider operations, authority, commands, and historical receipts remain unchanged unless direct code proof requires a separately admitted correction.
No public copy, content navigation, generic Fumadocs logic, deployment receipt, provider resource, DNS, release, or publication state changes.

Replace per-script process.env, Bun.file, JSON.parse, async/Promise, thrown/string errors, console, process.exitCode, and Effect.runPromise host paths.
Reuse or extend the existing deployment JSON/file boundary where it has semantic reuse; keep one-use verification logic inline.
Preserve exact candidate, stage, plan, provider, hosted, screenshot, teardown, and non-claim semantics.
Add deterministic success and failure fixtures for all five executables and update owning docs and task evidence.

Five BunRuntime executable adapters
Deterministic workflow verifier boundary tests
Updated deployment/testing owners and APP-IAC-001 validation receipt

Move ambient environment reads to Config-owned executable composition and inject typed process environment into the live Layer.

Use Effect collections for semantic membership and preserve exact deterministic ordering and classification.
Prove secrets cannot enter logs, receipts, errors, snapshots or child-process diagnostics.

Updated owner docs and APP-IAC-002 validation receipt

tasks.title: Prevent strict app and IaC boundary regressions
tasks.goal: Turn the repeated root causes into one small executable control with adversarial proof and bounded exceptions.
scope: Choose a focused custom lint rule or architecture test only after reviewing the final corrected syntax.
Reject stable prohibited forms in governed app/deployment runtime source without banning legitimate host adapters or test fixtures.

Add valid and invalid adversarial fixtures for direct environment access, manual JSON/file/runtime execution, raw promises, unmanaged runtime randomness/state, and permitted narrow adapters as applicable.
Wire the control once into the existing verification graph and document any named exception with owner, reason, carrying cost, review trigger and retirement condition.
outputs: Focused recurrence-prevention control
Adversarial fixtures
Root verification wiring
